title.narrative: Bangladesh Rohingya and Host Community Humanitarian Package

description.narrative: The Rohingya crisis is the largest and most complex humanitarian crisis in the Indo-Pacific region. As at January 2020 over 1.2 million people need humanitarian assistance in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, including both Rohingya refugees and impacted host communities. The Bangladesh Rohingya and Host Community Humanitarian Package (2020-2022) is the country level humanitarian response to this cross border crisis originating in Myanmar and causing large-scale displacement into Bangladesh. The Bangladesh package objective is to contribute to international efforts to meet humanitarian and protection needs and increase self-reliance and resilience of Rohingya and host populations in Bangladesh. The aim is to meet refugees and host communities’ basic needs; increase their self-reliance; build resilience and social cohesion; and improve the effectiveness of the humanitarian system. The total estimated investment value is $230m ($10m from global partnerships) over 3 years, starting in 2019-20.

title.narrative: The Evaluation of the AHP Bangladesh Humanitarian Response Phase III

description.narrative: Farmers in the village of Harashiya in Cox’s Bazar had been facing recurring losses in their paddy production due to blockages in their nearby canal, which was limiting irrigation. AHP partner, Caritas Bangladesh, re-excavated the canal, resulting in increased survival rates for the crops. Partners also provided 1,468 women with livelihoods training, building their capacity for ensuring food security in their households. Following host community training on homestead gardening and pit composting, AHP partner Oxfam reported that the income of project participants increased by BDT 6,179 per month on average.

In 2022, Australian Government partners UNFPA and IOM supported health systems strengthening in Bangladesh. UNFPA supported an emergency referral ambulance system (Matri Sheba) – a network of eight ambulances conducting emergency obstetric and newborn referrals from community to health facilities. A total of 6,696 emergency obstetric referrals were completed through this system in 2022. Led by Community Health Workers (CHWs), UNFPA strengthened referral pathways and the mechanisms that connect communities and lower-level facilities with referral-level facilities. ‍ IOM strengthened emergency preparedness and response capacity for public health emergencies, by strengthening the emergency and outbreak management capacity of national health facilities.

In 2022, Australian funding helped to provide 23,846 women and girl survivors of violence with services such as counselling, in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh This support was provided through our partners the AHP, BRAC, IOM, UNFPA, UNHCR and UN Women. AHP consortium partner, CARE, reported that support provided to women in camps 11, 12, and 14 resulted in these female participants being able to reduce instances of gender-based violence within their families.

In 2022, Australian funding helped to support 13,161 people to be immunised in the Rohingya camps and adjacent host communities in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. This assistance was delivered through multiple partners including the AHP, BRAC, IOM and UNICEF. No further reporting provided by partners to expand on immunisation reach/coverage.

In 2022, Australian funding supported emergency assistance to 1,421,347 individuals, including 18,580 persons living with a disability. This included food assistance, health services, protection, basic shelter and non-food items. Assistance was delivered through AHP, BRAC, IOM, UNFPA, UNHCR, UNICEF, UN Women and WFP. ‍ AHP partner Save the Children reported a retention rate of 83% and attendance rate of 91.5% among 8,270 students. WFP reported that resale of food assistance decreased by 10% between 2020 and 2022. Additionally, people supported with nutrition interventions had high recovery rates from malnutrition through its camp and host community program (95 and 98 percent).
